title: Order history shows the previous account after switching
ticket: Support: a customer switched to their business account and still saw their personal orders until they reloaded the page.

lines: export function OrderHistory({ userId }: { userId: string }) {

failing.test: OrderHistory › shows the new account's orders after userId changes
output: Unable to find an element with the text: Invoice B-2041

explanation.cause: The effect ran once on mount and never again: its dependency list left out userId.
explanation.why: Listing userId re-fetches when the account changes, and the cleanup flag already discards the old request's late answer. No list at all refetches on every render, and [orders] loops forever.

title: Cart total shows $0.30000000000000004
ticket: Screenshot from a customer: three 10-cent stickers, and the cart total reads $0.30000000000000004. Payments also rejected one order for an 'amount mismatch'.

lines: type CartItem = { name: string; priceCents: number; price: number; quantity: number };
/** The cart's total in dollars, for display and for the payment request. */
export function cartTotal(items: readonly CartItem[]): number {
const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.quantity, 0);
export function formatTotal(items: readonly CartItem[]): string {

fixes: const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.priceCents * item.quantity, 0) / 100;
const total = Math.round(items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.quantity, 0));
const total = Number(items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.quantity, 0).toFixed(1));
const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0) * items.length;

explanation.cause: Binary floating point can't represent 0.10 exactly, so summing dollar floats drifts.
explanation.why: Adding whole cents keeps every step exact and divides once at the end. Rounding to whole dollars or one decimal hides the drift by throwing money away, and the payment API would still see the wrong amount.

title: Retry checkout automatically when it times out
author: Web release bot (FE-2291)
description: Customers see 'Something went wrong' on transient timeouts. This retries the checkout request up to four times before showing the error, so most hiccups are invisible.

diff.text: export async function submitCheckout(cart: Cart): Promise<Order> {

explanation.cause: Each retry re-sends the charge immediately, with no backoff and no idempotency key.
explanation.why: When checkout slows down, every client turns one request into four at once, which makes the slowdown worse, and a timed-out charge that actually went through gets made again. Retries need jittered backoff, a budget, and an idempotency key the server dedupes on.

title: Lazy-load the analytics page
author: Maya Okonkwo
description: The analytics page pulls in a 400 KB charting library that every visitor downloads on the first load. Only staff open it, so this moves it into its own chunk.

explanation.cause: Nothing wrong: the page is code-split and wrapped in Suspense with a fallback.
explanation.why: lazy() wants a default export; mapping the named AnalyticsPage export to default keeps it working, and the Suspense fallback covers the load. Nobody else pays for the chart library.

title: Receipts are dated one month early
ticket: A customer paid on March 14 and the receipt page says 2/14/2026. Their accountant flagged it as a February charge.

lines: /** A short local date for receipts, like 3/14/2026. */

explanation.cause: getMonth() counts from 0, so March comes back as 2.
explanation.why: Adding one gives the calendar month. getUTCMonth is zero-based too, getDay is the day of the week, and || 12 only changes January.

title: Warn people a minute before their session expires
author: Tomas Reyes
description: People lose half-filled forms when the session times out. This calls onOneMinuteLeft from the existing countdown so the page can show a 'save your work' banner at 1:00.

diff.text: export function SessionTimer({ expiresInSeconds }: { expiresInSeconds: number }) {
export function SessionTimer({ expiresInSeconds, onOneMinuteLeft }: { expiresInSeconds: number; onOneMinuteLeft: () => void }) {

explanation.cause: The interval callback was created on the first render, so the remaining it checks is always the starting value. The warning never fires, or fires every second if the session starts at exactly 60.
explanation.why: The existing tick is safe because it uses the functional setRemaining. The new check needs the live value too: run it in a separate effect on [remaining], or check current inside the updater.

title: Search shows results for what you typed a moment ago
ticket: Typing 'lamp' quickly sometimes shows the results for 'lam', and they stay there until you type another letter. Happens most on slow mobile connections.

failing.test: SearchBox › keeps the latest query's results when responses arrive out of order
output: typed 'lam' then 'lamp'; the 'lam' response resolved last

explanation.cause: The cleanup aborts a controller whose signal never reaches the request, so the older 'lam' fetch still resolves and overwrites the newer results.
explanation.why: Passing controller.signal lets the cleanup cancel the stale request, which then rejects with AbortError and is ignored. A brand new controller is never aborted, and skipping the cache or trimming the query does nothing about ordering.

title: Badge invoices that are due today or overdue
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Adds 'Due today' and 'Overdue' badges to the invoice list so people pay before the late fee. Due dates come from the API as plain calendar days, so this compares date strings instead of timestamps.

diff.text: /** Invoices carry their due date as a plain calendar day, like "2026-10-10". */
export function isDueToday(dueDate: string, now = new Date()): boolean {
export function isOverdue(dueDate: string, now = new Date()): boolean {

explanation.cause: toISOString gives the UTC date, not the user's, so 'today' rolls over at UTC midnight.
explanation.why: In the evening for anyone west of UTC, an invoice due today shows as overdue, and just after midnight in the east it isn't due yet. Build the key from getFullYear, getMonth and getDate so it matches the local calendar day.

title: Flip the like button before the server answers
author: Jonah Whitfield
description: Liking a post waits a full round trip before the heart fills, which feels broken on mobile. This updates the cached post right away and puts it back if the request fails.

explanation.cause: Nothing wrong: the optimistic write is snapshotted first and rolled back on error.
explanation.why: Cancelling in-flight fetches stops a stale refetch from overwriting the optimistic heart, the copy keeps the snapshot untouched, and refetching on settle brings the like count back in line with the server.
